name: Two-block graph-state code with a transposed matching

provenance.construction: Additive CWS construction on two C_8 squared graphs, with cross matching pi=[0,1,2,3,4,5,7,6]. For graph-state generators K_i=X_i Z_(N(i)), take K_i K_(i+1) for i=0,...,6 in each block. The two block-even label subspaces give 14 independent weight-six checks.
references: Cross, Smith, Smolin and Zeng, Codeword Stabilized Quantum Codes, arXiv:0708.1021v4; IEEE Transactions on Information Theory 55, 433-438 (2009). https://arxiv.org/abs/0708.1021v4
Grassl, Bounds on additive quantum codes: [[16,2,6]] stored generator matrix. https://www.codetables.de/QECC.php?q=4&n=16&k=2
provenance.notes: Independently constructed instance within the established additive CWS framework; concrete code-space novelty is unverified. The known [[16,2,6]] means no unrestricted parameter record is claimed. This code is not obtained by relabeling a board entry. Fourteen independent weight-six checks, maximum qubit degree six, 84 incidences. The note includes a standalone reconstruction and exhaustive finite symplectic verification of distance five and a basis-independent non-LC-CSS argument. This is supplementary computational evidence, not an official exact certificate; distance.P.confidence remains upper_bound. No circuit, layout or LER claim. AI tools: GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol with OpenAI Codex. See notes/16-2-5.md.
